summary: The protected October 13 handoff records the Arch base-20261011.0.609700 amd64 donor manifest and distinguishes its metadata from unacquired or unaccepted package closure. It explicitly describes the common-base recipe as five staged unreviewed files with no source PR and no package checksum manifest. Losing those drafts does not lose the protected donor/input decision and does not create an accepted recipe. Docker Official Images metadata independently maps the same tag to archlinux-docker commit 1e7d9a2d495ffe76934a775b6bd68ac892a14c1b and Dockerfile.base; those GitLab file bytes were not inspected. Genuine donor package state, full maintained package-manager transaction and trusted archives remain required before build-ready acceptance. The host inventory and a language-specific consumer image cannot substitute for those inputs. Prepared source now pins that donor and the October12 core/extra snapshot, uses a full offline pacman transaction with trusted package signatures under a pending reconciled candidate policy, and rejects missing, extra, duplicate, unsafe-path, non-regular or byte-drifted checksum population before the package transaction. The expected complete final package inventory is itself checksum-bound. The source specification deliberately retains absent acquired inputs; supplied-population coverage cannot prove authentic transaction closure, runtime qualification, provisioning, publication or installed adoption.
title: Pinned Arch donor survives loss of uncommitted common-base draft
